## (A) All-T MDE at baseline, per organ {#fig6a}

```{r fig6a-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6a"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6a-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="24%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c(
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_blood.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_spleen.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_LN.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_colonLP.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_colonepi.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_smallintestineLP.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_smallintestineepi.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_lung.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_kidney.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_liver.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_skin.png",
  "assets/Figure6/6a_MDE_baseline_mammarygland.png"))
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6A.** Gallery of all-T MDEs showing the distribution of T cells at
baseline across organs, coloured by lineage. Each organ is capped at 10,000
cells so that visual density reflects composition rather than sequencing depth.
The five sparsely sampled sites are shown in
[Extended Data Figure 8](FigureS8.html).
:::

## (B) Cluster proportions across organs {#fig6b}

```{r fig6b-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6b"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6b-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6b_DotPlot_level2_by_organ_baseline.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6B.** Dot plot showing the proportion of immgenT clusters across organs
at baseline. Colour intensity reflects the mean proportion of each cluster
within its lineage, and dot size the total number of profiled cells. Computing
the proportion within lineage rather than within sample makes tissues with very
different lineage composition comparable.
:::

## (C) Cluster proportions across perturbations in the colon {#fig6c}

```{r fig6c-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure6.R", "6c"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig6c-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure6/6c_DotPlot_level2_by_condition_colon.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 6C.** The same quantity across immune perturbations in the colon lamina
propria, with baseline as the reference row. Perturbations redistribute cells
among the same set of clusters rather than producing new ones.
:::
